title: Synthesis grants
amount_raw: Synthesis groups can claim up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants
eligibility_summary: The main applicant must hold BES membership (other working-group members need not). Groups must be diverse in career stage, gender, ethnicity, institution type and country, must include international participation, and must NOT be formed entirely of members from academic institutions — networks across universities, research institutes, NGOs, industry and government are expected, including members from where the data originated. Applicants must obtain all relevant permits.
summary: £30k towards forming a new two-year synthesis group (8-15 individuals) to fast-track innovative and impactful ecological research, with an expectation of lasting networks, open synthesis datasets and synthesis publications.

title: Pedagogical research and development grants
amount_raw: Projects can be awarded up to £5;000
eligibility_summary:
Must have BES membership.
Projects should be a maximum of 12 months
These grants have no geographical restrictions and are open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (i.e. from early years to life-long learning within formal or informal educational settings.
Applications can also be from those in an industry that would like to explore the impact of new teaching ideas.
These grants are awarded to individuals, not organisations.
Funding is unavailable for work that will form part of a degree/masters/PhD/fellowship.
Applicants are responsible for obtaining all relevant permits and permissions required to undertake the proposed work.
We will not award more than one grant to any applicant in any year and no more than two grants in any five years.
Failure to submit a satisfactory report at the end of a grant will mean the grantee is ineligible to apply for further grants.

summary:
The grant will facilitate research informing teaching and learning practices which improve learners’ experience while promoting excellence in teaching.
We aim to support our members involved in education to ensure that ecological education continues to be inspiring, innovative and relevant to learners.
By funding research on education methods within ecology, we would like to develop evidence to inform teaching and learning practices that improve the student experience. Recognising and supporting educational research will also promote excellence in teaching and encourage those not currently involved in educational research to engage.
The projects awarded should aim to do one or more of the following:
Provide evidence-based examples of innovative and effective practice in learning and teaching.
Systematically review existing practices to produce evidence-informed recommendations.
Explore emerging areas of education research to identify future needs/practices.
Disseminate best practices in teaching and learning to other practitioners

title: Connecting ecologists with other disciplines grants
amount_raw: Grant awards of up to £20;000 can be claimed from the applicant
eligibility_summary:
Must have BES membership.
These grants are awarded to individuals, not organisations.
These grants are for ecologists only to work in a distinctly different sector compared to their current one.
Placements can be full-time or part-time, and can be up to 12 months long.
Applicants are responsible for obtaining all relevant permits and permissions required to undertake the proposed work.
We will not award more than one grant to any applicant in any year and no more than two grants in any five years.
This grant is open to those who:
Are PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations (eg government agencies) who would like to develop interdisciplinary skills and are trying to influence other disciplines to increase ecological understanding.
Have their employer/supervisor approval to step out of current activities during the placement period
Have a willing host organisation/department who will collaborate on the grant application.
Undergraduates and masters students are not eligible to apply
summary: We aim to support our members involved in education to ensure that ecological education continues to be inspiring. Interdisciplinary work is the process of integrating knowledge and ideas from different subjects or fields.

title: Outreach and engagement grants
eligibility_summary:
We will not award more than one grant to any applicant in any year and no more than two grants in any five years. 

All Grants must be for projects that meet at least one of the top-level BES aims:

Communicate evidence-based messaging for what ecology is, how nature works, and the use of ecological science as a solution to local and global challenges.
Raise awareness and public understanding of ecological careers, their relevance and importance, breadth, and diversity, and show that anybody can become an ecologist.
Share how individuals can take action to benefit the environment, themselves, and society.
Increase the ability of others to deliver the above aims through outreach and engagement activities.

additional: 

Your proposal must be aimed at a non-academic audience, and all projects must clearly demonstrate direct interaction with them. They should also show evidence of links to the research community at regional, national and international levels, where appropriate.

[moved from exclusion_reason, 2026-08-26] Applications will NOT be considered for:

Staff salaries (one-off costs that are relevant to completing the event e.g. sub-contracting for logo design, will be considered)
Training courses not associated with developing skills in communicating the science of ecology for a public-facing audience
Projects aimed solely at delivering curriculum to school children.
Projects that are delivered to a small number (1-2) schools in a school setting where other members of the public can’t engage.
summary:
Engaging public audiences with the relevance and importance of ecological science and careers is vital.
This grant will support BES members to deliver independent outreach, public engagement and science communication activities that engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science or enhance the experience and skills of others to communicate ecology with public audiences.
The grant will support diverse formats that reach and engage public audiences in innovative, creative and impactful ways, whether through in-person events, digital formats, or physical resources.
notes: Own page: 'Round 2 opens 8 June and closes 8 September 2026' — open on the snapshot date. The award may be used as part-funding for a larger project involving other sponsors, unlike the Small Research Grants. Membership gate (restricted). amount_raw semicolon substitutes for the comma in '£2,000'.

title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
eligibility_summary:
Must be a BES member, you can be at any stage in your research career.
Must be a citizen of and based in* the Global South. A full list of all Global South countries can be found on the United Nations Finance Centre for South-South Cooperation. We have chosen this list as it represents countries with less resource for ecological research.
Must be travelling from and returning to the country you are based in the Global South
Must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting (this can include workshops, research presentations, posters, etc). Evidence of abstract submission must be provided as part of the application process.
Must be at least three years since you were last awarded a BES Training and Travel Grant.
summary:
This grant supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK. Funding is intended to support travel from the applicant’s country of residence in the Global South to the UK and return travel to that country after the meeting. 

The maximum grant award is £1000. This can cover any costs that are directly related to attending the meeting, such as registration costs, transport, food and accommodation.
notes: Own page: 'these grants will open on 17 July 2026 and close on 8 September 2026' — open on the 2026-08-16 snapshot. NOTE this scheme runs on its own calendar (opening 17 July) rather than the standard Round 1/Round 2 cycle, but happens to share the 8 September closing date. Geographically restricted to the Global South, which is why restricted is tagged; this is the practical expression of the BES commitment that at least 51% of funding goes to ecologists in low and lower-middle income countries. A 2025 edition page (content/bes-annual-meeting-grants-2025) is a past-round distractor and is not a separate row.

title: Training and travel grants
amount_raw: Grants of up to £500 are available
eligibility_summary:
Applicants must be a BES member AND a PhD student or postgraduate researcher registered on a postgraduate research degree programme. Research staff, research assistants, postdoctoral researchers, undergraduates, master's students and graduates who have completed their degree are all explicitly ineligible. A maximum of two places per training course may be funded, and no more than two applicants from the same institution may attend the same meeting or conference. Grants are paid in retrospect, so the applicant must pay the organiser at the time of booking.

Work in scientific areas within our remit (the science of ecology) and of relevance to the training course or meeting they are applying to attend.
Give a presentation if attending a meeting. For example, poster presentations, delivering workshops, delivering a plenary talk, etc. You will need to upload evidence of abstract submission or acceptance as part of the application process.
summary: These grants help PhD students and postgraduate researchers* to meet the costs of specialist field training courses and to network and publicise their research by presenting their work at workshops and conferences.
notes: The ONE BES scheme that is forthcoming rather than open on this snapshot: it runs on a separate three-round calendar and its own page states 'Round 3 opens 24 August and closes 8 September 2026' — eight days after the 2026-08-16 snapshot. A stated future opening date makes it in scope as forthcoming, per the Leverhulme precedent. Both dates recorded: next_open_date 2026-08-24 and the round deadline 2026-09-08.
